_comment: Seeded from a prior manual migration project (50+ VMs, 5 batches, 2 standalone ESXi hosts). Each entry's `mechanically_triggerable` field is honest about whether Phase 3's rule-based orchestrator can detect the trigger condition itself (from structured tool output) or whether it genuinely requires Phase 4's LLM/vision judgment (e.g. classifying a screenshot). Phase 8: any new pattern confirmed via human escalation during a real run should be proposed for addition here, with human confirmation, in the same shape.

issues.trigger_description: FreeBSD guest boots to a `mountroot>` prompt after migration. Root cause: source VM used VMware BusLogic/SCSI (`da0` device naming); QEMU's SATA/AHCI emulation enumerates the same disk as `ad4` (older FreeBSD/ATA driver) or `ada0` (newer FreeBSD/AHCI-CAM driver) instead.
issues.detection_note: Requires reading a boot screenshot or serial console text to recognize the mountroot prompt -- not decidable from register_vm/convert_vm_disk output alone. Phase 3 cannot auto-apply this; it's seeded here for Phase 4.
issues.fix_description: At the mountroot> prompt: use '?' to list actual valid boot devices if unsure, then specify 'ufs:/dev/ad4s1a' or 'ufs:/dev/ada0s1a' (whichever matches what was listed). Boot through once, then permanently fix /etc/fstab (da0 -> actual device) and confirm /boot/loader.conf has no stale vfs.root.mountfrom override.
confirmed_on: one of two IPv6-TestBed FreeBSD VMs (ad4 variant)

issues.trigger_description: Linux guest running a GNOME/Wayland desktop hangs at a black screen on the primary console after the display manager loads, when using Proxmox's default 'std' VGA adapter.
issues.detection_note: Requires reading a boot screenshot to distinguish 'genuinely black, no signal' from other failure modes -- Phase 4 concern.
issues.fix_description: qm set <vmid> --vga qxl, then retry boot.

issues.trigger_description: Same visible symptom as gdm_wayland_black_screen_qxl (black screen after boot) but with a DIFFERENT root cause: GDM's Wayland compositor grabs the display exclusively at the DRM/KMS level -- this is not a video-adapter-capability problem (the console works fine on a text VT), so changing --vga does not always resolve it, and ctrl-alt-F2 VT-switching does not escape it either.
issues.detection_note: Distinguishing this from gdm_wayland_black_screen_qxl requires trying qxl first and confirming (via another boot observation) whether the black screen persists -- itself a judgment call needing Phase 4. Included as a documented SECOND candidate fix, not a replacement for the qxl entry above, because both are independently verified real fixes for related-but-distinct symptoms.
issues.fix_description: Offline (VM stopped): virt-customize -a <raw-disk-path> --run-command 'systemctl set-default multi-user.target'. This makes the VM boot straight to a text console instead of attempting the GUI at all. Trade-off vs. the qxl fix: this disables the GUI entirely rather than fixing display rendering -- only appropriate when text-console access is an acceptable outcome for this VM's purpose (it was, for testbed/infrastructure VMs in the source project). Requires the guest's UFS/ext filesystem to be writable by the host's libguestfs appliance offline -- confirmed to work for Linux ext4 guests; confirmed NOT to work for FreeBSD UFS2 guests in this same project (the Linux UFS kernel driver used by the libguestfs appliance is read-only for UFS2 -- see freebsd_da0_ada0_mountroot's fix, which is applied live from within the guest instead for exactly this reason).
issues.caution: A task spec in the source project once incorrectly cited this fix as being the same as '--vga qxl'. It is not -- verify empirically per-VM rather than trusting either fix's description as guaranteed to apply, and do not assume one fix's prior success implies the other will also work.

issues.trigger_description: path_resolver's appliance-risk heuristic (name/annotation pattern match against known SD-WAN/IOS-XE/vendor-appliance product names, e.g. vManage/vBond/vSmart/C8000v/CSR1000v, combined with a generic guest-OS string) flags a VM as appliance_risk=likely_appliance.
issues.fix_description: No fix -- this tool's plain disk-conversion pipeline does not support vendor appliance images. Exclude from the migration plan by default.
issues.known_limitation: Name/annotation heuristics are best-effort. A VM named something generic (e.g. 'NetconfServer') that is ACTUALLY a vendor appliance (confirmed real case: an IOS-XE virtual router registered under exactly that generic name in the source project) will NOT be caught by this heuristic and will need to be caught by a human noticing the boot failure pattern instead (stuck at a vendor-specific bootloader stage, e.g. '%IOSXEBOOT-...' banner, with flat disk I/O and 0% CPU well past a normal boot window). Treat an unexplained early-bootloader hang on an unfamiliar guest as reason to escalate, not just retry.

issues.trigger_description: path_resolver.resolve()'s power_state comes back 'poweredOn' (or 'suspended') for a VM selected for migration.
issues.fix_description: None -- this is always a human decision (is this VM actively in use? safe to skip? should someone coordinate a maintenance window?), never inferable from ESXi/Proxmox telemetry alone.

issues.trigger_description: register_vm's result has disk_imported=true but disk_attached=false (confirmed via independent qm config read-back, not the qm set exit code) -- the exact silent-failure mode this whole tool exists to catch.
issues.fix_description: Retry the `qm set --sataN <storage>:<vmid>/vm-<vmid>-disk-0.raw` attachment step once, then re-verify via qm config. If it fails a second time, escalate -- do not retry indefinitely.

issues.trigger_description: check_staging_capacity reports sufficient=false for a planned copy.
issues.fix_description: None safe to automate -- freeing space or expanding storage are both real infrastructure decisions.
issues.note: Root filesystem (96GB) was filled to 100% twice during the manual project by staging in the wrong location. capacity_check.assert_staging_on_bulk_storage() prevents the location mistake structurally; this rule catches the remaining case of genuinely not enough room even on the correct storage.

issues.fix_description: None safe to automate -- could indicate a corrupted source disk, a wrong snapshot descriptor was targeted, or a genuinely resized disk. Needs a human look before trusting the output.

issues.trigger_description: detect_collisions reports has_collisions=true for the planned batch.
issues.fix_description: No action needed beyond logging -- copy_engine's per-VM staging subdirectories make actual data loss from a filename collision structurally impossible regardless of how many VMs share a source .vmdk filename. This entry exists for audit visibility, not because intervention is required.
confirmed_on: 4-way collision: IPv6_WIN10-HOST.vmdk across 4 unrelated Windows VMs
5-way collision: IPv6_RefDUT_2.vmdk across one testbed batch
